# ui::Bitmap

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

A CPU bitmap, 4 bytes per pixel: RGBA with straight alpha unless made in another [PixelFormat](namespace-ui.md#pixelformat).

The picture type everything image-shaped uses: [ImageSource](image-source.md) and the [Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage) element, [Icon](../controls/icon.md#uiicon), [PersonPicture](../controls/person-picture.md#uipersonpicture), [IconSource::bitmap()](icon-source.md#bitmap), the clipboard, and pixel tests, which capture into one and check it with [compare()](namespace-ui.md#compare). PNG encodes and decodes byte for byte the same on every platform. [decode()](#decode) and [read()](#read) handle photos (JPEG, GIF and the other formats the system's image codecs read) with optional downscaling and EXIF orientation. A value type: copying copies the pixels.

A renderer that writes premultiplied BGRA can draw straight into a bitmap made in that format, through [bytes()](#bytes), and the picture then reaches the screen with no pass over its pixels. [get()](#get), [set()](#set) and the encoders work in either format.

Example: 
```cpp
// Load a photo for display, bounded to 1024px and upright.
ui::Bitmap photo = ui::Bitmap::read("holiday.jpg", {.max_width = 1024, .max_height = 1024});
window.set_content(ui::Image{.source = std::move(photo), .stretch = ui::Stretch::Uniform});

// Build one by hand, e.g. a color swatch for a palette export, and save it as PNG.
ui::Bitmap swatch{16, 16, ui::colors::White};
swatch.set(0, 0, ui::Color::from_rgba(255, 0, 0));
swatch.write_png("swatch.png"); // lossless: read_png() gives back the same pixels

// A page a PDF renderer draws right into the bitmap's bytes, shown as they are. Here the
// page is filled opaque white, the same in premultiplied BGRA.
ui::Bitmap page{612, 792, ui::PixelFormat::Bgra8Premultiplied};
std::ranges::fill(page.bytes(), std::uint8_t{0xFF});
```

## Bitmap

```cpp
Bitmap() = default
```

An empty (0x0) image.

## Bitmap

```cpp
Bitmap(int width, int height, const Color& fill = colors::Transparent)
```

A [`width`](#width) x [`height`](#height) image, every pixel [`fill`](#fill) (transparent by default).

## Bitmap

```cpp
Bitmap(int width, int height, PixelFormat format)
```

A [`width`](#width) x [`height`](#height) image in [`format`](#format), every pixel transparent: zero bytes, ready for a renderer to draw into through [bytes()](#bytes).

## width

```cpp
int width() const
```

Width in pixels; 0 when empty.

## height

```cpp
int height() const
```

Height in pixels; 0 when empty.

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

True when either dimension is zero (nothing to draw).

## format

```cpp
PixelFormat format() const
```

How the bytes are laid out; Rgba8 unless the bitmap was made in another format.

## converted

```cpp
Bitmap converted(PixelFormat format) const
```

The same picture with its bytes in [`format`](#format); a copy when it is already in it.

## bytes

```cpp
std::span<const std::uint8_t> bytes() const
```

The pixel bytes in [format()](#format)'s layout, row-major, 4 per pixel, width * 4 per row.

## bytes

```cpp
std::span<std::uint8_t> bytes()
```

The pixel bytes, writable; width * height * 4 of them. Asking for them counts as a change to the pixels ([content_id()](#content_id)).

## content_id

```cpp
std::uint64_t content_id() const
```

A number that stays the same while the pixels do and is never reused for other pixels: a copy shares it until either side is written to ([fill()](#fill), [set()](#set), [blend()](#blend), the writable [bytes()](#bytes)). A renderer keeps the copy it uploaded to the GPU under it.

## fill

```cpp
void fill(const Color& c)
```

Sets every pixel to `c` (a replace, not a blend).

## set

```cpp
void set(int x, int y, const Color& c)
```

Replaces the pixel, ignoring what was there.

## get

```cpp
Color get(int x, int y) const
```

Reads a pixel back as a [Color](../core/color.md), with straight alpha in either format.

## blend

```cpp
void blend(int x, int y, const Color& c, std::uint8_t coverage)
```

Source-over composite of `c` at coverage (0..255) onto the existing pixel.

## encode_png

```cpp
std::vector<std::uint8_t> encode_png() const
```

The image as PNG bytes, identical on every platform.

## write_png

```cpp
void write_png(const std::filesystem::path& path) const
```

[encode_png()](#encode_png) written to `path`. Throws std::runtime_error if the file can't be written.

## encode_jpeg

```cpp
std::vector<std::uint8_t> encode_jpeg(int quality = 90) const
```

Baseline JPEG at `quality` (1..100). Alpha is dropped; JPEG has none.

## oriented

```cpp
Bitmap oriented(ImageOrientation orientation) const
```

This image turned upright, given the `orientation` it was stored with.

## scaled_to_fit

```cpp
Bitmap scaled_to_fit(int max_width, int max_height) const
```

This image shrunk to fit inside `max_width` × `max_height` (zero: unconstrained), aspect ratio kept, by area averaging with alpha weighting, so a transparent pixel's color doesn't bleed into its neighbors. Never enlarges: an image that already fits comes back as is. The result keeps the format.

## decode_png

```cpp
static Bitmap decode_png(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& data)
```

Decodes PNG bytes, identically on every platform. Throws std::runtime_error if `data` is not a readable PNG.

## read_png

```cpp
static Bitmap read_png(const std::filesystem::path& path)
```

[decode_png()](#decode_png) of the file at `path`. Throws std::runtime_error if it can't be read.

## decode

```cpp
static Bitmap decode(std::span<const std::uint8_t> data, const ImageDecodeOptions& options = {})
```

Decodes an encoded image held in memory. Throws std::runtime_error if it can't.

## read

```cpp
static Bitmap read(const std::filesystem::path& path, const ImageDecodeOptions& options = {})
```

Decodes the file at `path`. Any file name opens, whatever characters it holds. Throws std::runtime_error if the file can't be read or decoded. Thread-safe and meant to be called from worker threads, which need no setup for it.

## read_thumbnail

```cpp
static Bitmap read_thumbnail(const std::filesystem::path& path, int max_edge)
```

[read()](#read) into a `max_edge` × `max_edge` box, upright.

## read_orientation

```cpp
static ImageOrientation read_orientation(std::span<const std::uint8_t> data)
```

The EXIF orientation recorded in an encoded JPEG or TIFF, Normal when there is none. Reads only the header; [decode()](#decode)/read() already apply it unless told not to.
